**What I do:** Nothing is due today. That's the exam. Old me treats a quiet Wednesday as permission to go dark till teatime. New me knows the quiet is where the habit either lives or dies.

So, 8:12, Callum gets the details — plain, no comedy, no exit:

> "Sort code 20-XX-XX, account ending 4471. Standing order, reference 'van'. Friday's fine. Good lad. — E"

No joke, because jokes were how £9,400 went invisible. And at lunch, from the van, one line to Mare — not a headline, a fact:

> "Sent Cal the account details. £75 standing order starts Friday. Said I'd tell you it's moving, so: it's moving. — E"

Not because she audits. Because I say things out loud now.

Mum's the harder post. "Don't ring me about it" — she said don't ring, she never said don't answer. So I text, once, and honour the shape of her:

> "Heard. Not ringing. For the record: he'd have said the house is quieter because you talk less and mean more. Door's open Sunday if the quiet gets loud. — E"
